name: GitHub Workflow Rulebook
summary: The repository, branches, commits, pull requests, CI, quality gates, deploys and releases.
check: CI and quality workflows green on the main branch; branch protection on; Dependabot running.

rules.title: One repository per site
rules.text: Each site has its own repository with a clear name, a description, topics and the live website URL set.

rules.title: A real README
rules.text: What the site is, the live URL, how to install, run, build and deploy (commands that actually exist in `package.json`), where content is edited, and the tech stack.

rules.title: Ignore what must not be committed
rules.text: `.gitignore` for `node_modules`, build output, `.env*` (except `.env.example`), OS and editor files, logs, local caches.

rules.title: `.env.example`
rules.text: Every environment variable the project needs, with placeholder values and a comment. Real secrets live in GitHub Actions secrets or the host's secret store (`SEC-04`).

rules.title: Consistent formatting
rules.text: `.editorconfig`, a formatter (Prettier or the stack's equivalent) and a linter configured in the repo and run in CI.

rules.title: `main` is always deployable
rules.text: Work happens on short branches (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`), merged by pull request.

rules.title: Conventional commits
rules.text: `feat:`, `fix:`, `style:`, `perf:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `ci:`, with a short imperative summary. One logical change per commit.

rules.title: Pull requests with a checklist
rules.text: Every PR uses the template: what changed, screenshots at mobile and desktop, XSlop passes touched, how it was tested.

rules.title: Protected `main`
rules.text: Branch protection (or a ruleset): pull request required, CI must pass, no force pushes. For a solo project, at least require CI.

rules.title: CI on every push and PR
rules.text: Install with a lockfile, lint, type-check, run tests if any, build.

rules.title: Quality gates
rules.text: Lighthouse CI with budgets (performance, accessibility, SEO, best practices), an accessibility check (axe or pa11y), a link checker, and `scripts/xslop-scan.mjs` for slop patterns.

rules.title: Preview deploys
rules.text: Each PR gets a preview URL (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages) so changes are reviewed in a browser, not only in code.

rules.title: Automated deploy from `main`
rules.text: GitHub Pages, Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare deploy on merge; the hosting config lives in the repo (`vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`, `wrangler.toml` or the Pages workflow).

rules.title: Dependency and security automation
rules.text: Dependabot (or Renovate) for npm and GitHub Actions, secret scanning and push protection on, CodeQL or another code scan for apps with a backend (`SEC-14`).

rules.title: Releases
rules.text: Tag versions (`v1.0.0`) at launch and at major changes, with release notes generated from the commits.

rules.title: Issue and PR templates
rules.text: A bug template (steps, expected, actual, device, screenshot) and a feature template, so feedback after launch arrives in a usable shape.

rules.title: Semantic versions
rules.text: Releases follow semantic versioning (major.minor.patch), so it is clear what a change means.

rules.title: A licence when the code is public
rules.text: Public repositories state a licence (MIT, Apache-2.0) or say clearly that all rights are reserved.

rules.title: CODEOWNERS on team projects
rules.text: A `CODEOWNERS` file asks the right people to review changes in their area.

rules.title: Force-pushing to main
rules.text: Never rewrite the history of `main`. Revert with a new commit instead.

rules.title: Committing generated files
rules.text: No build output, `node_modules`, caches or large binaries in Git. Large media goes to a CDN or Git LFS.

rules.title: Long-lived branches
rules.text: Branches live days, not months. Merge small changes often to avoid painful conflicts.
